transcript.text: I'm losing my mind. Should I fire a
client that makes up 50% of my revenue?
They're a nightmare, disorganized
records, last minute requests every
week, urgent messages every weekend.
Last month, I was up until 2:00 a.m.
three nights in a row because they
dumped a box of receipts on me the day
before their filing deadline. Everyone
says drop them, but they're half of my
income. So, are my only options happy
but broke or stressed but paid?
>> No, you're in a rock and hard place
situation, but it's of your own making.
And so, two changes. Number one is if
you cut your income in half, we never
actually walked that through, which is
if I cut it in half, can I survive? If
so, then yeah, you can fire the client
and then you survive on half your
income, which is why not being so
aggressive with your lifestyle is
important so you can be defensive with
the business and then build it the right
[music] way. The second element that I
would say is if you don't want to give
up all the income, then you just need to
have stronger boundaries. Now, you can
have that if you have a little bit of
leverage over the customer. So, if
you're doing some specific services that
they can't do themselves, which I'm
guessing given the amount that they're
demanding from you, they probably can't
do it themselves or they would have
already found somebody. And so, you can
say, "Hey, listen, we need to reset our
agreement in terms of how we're going to
work. I will work between these times,
and this is the scope that I work
within. This is what you can expect from
me in terms of turnaround. If that
doesn't work for you, that's fine. I'll
happily continue to work for you for the
next quarter or so so you can find
somebody else." Call that the
intermediary. You can still set those
boundaries and say that's the way it's
going to be, and then you can continue
to work under this new agreement or
arrangement. Now, if they don't want
that, then that's up to them, but you
keep to your boundaries. And then that
will give you the time to go find
another customer. But, I would say any
of these three scenarios get you out of
your current condition without worrying
about like this is my life forever.
